body.prose:
A slot can read more than one holon: what an expression gathers. An expression is a function given what it takes, data held in a body like any other, and the engine evaluates it to the holons it gathers, in the field's order. It is a holon, `{ $ref: H }`, a set of one; a call, `{ call: P, with: [ … ] }`, the function P given its arguments; or, within a function of one's own, `{ arg: i }`, what it was given. Every function is a holon of the type Function. Glass's own are native, run by the engine: Everything; Type, the instances of the types given; Children of and Parents of, what the holons given point to and what points to them; Text, what contains each word given; Store; Has a name; Is a type; And, Or and Not; and Group by. Each takes sets, which are expressions, so they compose as deep as one likes, Not: Children of: Type: Brief as it reads, or words, as a store's key or an axis. A function of one's own gives an expression over what it is given, so it is called as glass's are and stands beside them. Held in a mount, an expression is what the mount gives, and a component may gather in what it reads, so the same field can be looked at from as many angles as there are expressions, each drawn by whatever takes it.

Gathered, a set is flat, and a flat field is never what one wants to see. So Group by gives what it is given in collections besides, one for each value along an axis: type, parent or store. Each collection is itself an expression, the first narrowed by one value and grouped again automatically, so it opens like any place, in layers; layer by layer, the field is entered as it is made. Grouped automatically, the field chooses: for whatever is gathered it takes the axis that gives a few groups, three to a dozen, covering most of it, and where nothing splits a set, or every holon shares a value, it is given as it is. The root gives the field's roots: what nothing references, `Not(Children of(Everything))`, a pure expression and no function of its own. A holon that holds others is their group, so the field shows only the tops of its trees, a few dozen holons, each opened to go down; all of glass's briefs stand under one of them, Glass. Grouped by type, a holon nothing holds still collects under what it is, as orphans would. References build direction, from what holds to what is held; instanceship, from an instance to its type, groups crosswise and makes nothing anyone's child, so types do not swallow their instances.

```ts
Group by(Not(Children of(Everything)), "type")
// opened: Function (8), Component (6), Type (4), Mount (2), Brief (1: Glass), …
```

*The author's, 2026-11-03: expressions are just data, so no language is invented; open the power to look upon data from different angles, which is what the reader will become. The forms the session's. A form for what a holon holds, by key, was let go the same day as convoluted: a holon's parts are its own to open. Grouping the author's, the same day: expressions are grouping, expressions are locations, in layers, a collection opened to see what is inside; if nothing is chosen, everything grouped by the strongest, and play welcome to see what works. The axes and how strength is weighed the session's, a first try. Programs the author's, that night: an expression is taking a program and putting something into it; set operations are programs too, not reserved functionality, so one can add one's own just the same; held by and holds are simply parents and children; and not is needed. OpenLight had its core verbs as native programs, discoverable and called like any other; glass takes that, and sets as what they take, so they compose. Functions apart from programs the author's, the next day: a function is pure and used in what is drawn, a program is run and its return kept with its run, so a function's result is never stored; both first class. The roots the author's, the same night: a group of holons is a holon, so looking upon the field one sees only the roots of the trees its references make; orphans still collect under their type; written as a pure expression.*
body.title: Looking from many angles
